title: Traits
summary: Defining shared behaviour with traits, implementing them for your types and for existing ones, default methods, traits as parameters with impl Trait and generic bounds, returning impl Trait, associated types and constants, supertraits, the orphan rule, and blanket implementations.

cards.q: What is a default method in a trait?
cards.a:
A method with a body in the trait, which implementers get for free and may override

`describe` in `Shape` is a default method: `Circle` keeps it, while `Rect` overrides it with its own version.

The orphan rule: neither the trait nor the type is defined in your crate

You may implement a trait for a type only if one of them is yours; wrap the `Vec` in your own struct (a newtype) instead.

cards.q: A function takes `items: &[S]` with `S: Shape`. Can it receive a mix of circles and squares?
cards.a:
No: `S` is one type per call; mixing needs `dyn Shape` trait objects

A generic parameter is filled in with a single type for each call; `&[Box<dyn Shape>]` can hold different shapes.
